rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis applies high strain-rate sliding deformation to a single-phase CoCrFeMnNi alloy, whereas the target uses thermal aging of an as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (mechanical deformation vs. thermal aging) on different material systems.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high strain-rate sliding at moderately elevated temperature in ultra-high vacuum, while the target uses static thermal aging at 600°C and 750°C in air. The regimes are completely different (dynamic deformation vs. static aging), with no overlap in specific conditions.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes dynamic grain refinement, grain boundary amorphization, and nanocavitation leading to intergranular decohesion. The target mechanism involves L12 ordering in FCC domains, elevated APBE, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries. These are entirely different classes of mechanism (grain boundary cavitation vs. ordering-induced planar slip and phase boundary cracking).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced fracture toughness under high strain-rate deformation compared to a coarse-grained baseline. The target predicts a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition with minimum ductility at 600°C aging and recovery at 750°C. The predicted property (toughness/ductility) and direction (brittle behavior) are broadly similar, but the specific pattern (monotonic vs. non-monotonic) and the comparison baseline differ.
